Because expression ranking establishes discovery but not CAR-T suitability, we then applied explicit nomination gates: a systemic-safety score integrating whole-body GTEx transcriptomics with Human Protein Atlas protein-level evidence; a membrane-topology tractability gate distinguishing antibody-accessible single-pass and GPI-anchored ectodomains from multi-pass transporters and tail-anchored proteins; and a safety × coverage metric. Under stringent thresholds (combined safety ≥0.55, tumor-cell detection fraction ≥50%, safety × coverage ≥0.30), no Tier A antigen qualified. Ubiquitously expressed antigens were correctly demoted, including the tetraspanin CD9 (53.2% tumor-cell coverage but pan-tissue protein expression and high plasma abundance), and the highest-ranked transporter SLC7A2 was demoted by multi-pass topology (largest extracellular loop 38 aa) despite favorable transcriptomic safety. Leukemia inhibitory factor receptor (LIFR), a single-pass type I receptor with a contiguous 789-aa ectodomain, was the only antibody-tractable nominee for experimental follow-up yet remained liability laden (combined safety 0.41; safety × coverage 0.135) and is not a validated target. Cross-dataset expression overlap (93.3%) reflected mRNA reproducibility, not CAR-T validity or clinical validation, and generic-antibody docking was exploratory only. All findings are transcriptomic and require surface-level confirmation. This work contributes a reproducible meningioma surfaceome atlas and a transferable nomination framework and shows that rigorous gating leaves no single antigen with a favorable safety × coverage × tractability profile, motivating bispecific and logic-gated CAR-T strategies.

title: Sulforaphane Attenuates Ulcerative Colitis by Activating Nrf2 and Suppressing the NLRP3/IL-1β Inflammasome Axis.
abstract: Ulcerative Colitis (UC) is driven by disrupted epithelial barrier function and chronic inflammation, yet the interaction between oxidative stress and inflammasome signaling remains unclear. This study investigated whether Nrf2 expression correlates with NLRP3 inflammasome activity in intestinal epithelial cells under inflammatory conditions and whether the natural Nrf2 activator, Sulforaphane (SFN), modulates this axis. A UC-like inflammatory state was established in Caco-2 cells using a cytokine cocktail (TNF-α, LPS, IFN-γ, IL-1β). Nrf2 was silenced using siRNA, and SFN was administered for activate Nrf2. Gene and protein expression were assessed by qPCR, ELISA, and Western blot. Public bulk and single-cell RNA-seq datasets from UC patients were analyzed to validate clinical relevance. Cytokine stimulation significantly reduced Nrf2 expression while upregulating NLRP3, IL-1β, and IL-18 (p < 0.001). Nrf2 knockdown was associated with enhanced inflammasome activation, as evidenced by increased levels of NLRP3, caspase-1, and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Conversely, SFN pretreatment restored Nrf2 expression and markedly suppressed NLRP3 and IL-18 expression (p < 0.01 to p < 0.001). Multiomic analyses of UC patient samples confirmed an inverse expression pattern between Nrf2 and NLRP3 signaling pathways. These findings indicate that reduced Nrf2 expression is strongly associated with enhanced NLRP3 inflammasome activation in inflamed intestinal epithelial cells. Pharmacologic activation of Nrf2 by SFN correlates with restored redox balance and attenuated inflammation, supporting the Nrf2-NLRP3 axis as a potential therapeutic target warranting further investigation. Limitations include use of a single cell line and lack of in vivo validation. This study provides correlative evidence for a redox-inflammasome axis in UC pathogenesis and suggests that further investigation of SFN as a candidate therapeutic approach is warranted.

title: Integrated pituitary adaptations to the low estrogen state.
abstract: Estrogen's broad trophic effects on anterior pituitary function are not fully understood. The compound 4-vinyl cyclohexene diepoxide (VCD) induces early ovarian failure and reduced E2 production, which may differentially affect anterior pituitary cells. We recently identified transcriptomic changes in pituitary gonadotropes at the single-cell level in females treated with VCD for 20 days, which were acyclic, with low serum estradiol (E2) levels and 8-12-fold increases in gonadotropins 138 days later. We tested vehicle-control and VCD-treated female mice in metabolic cages and assayed serum hormone levels by EIA, and pituitary cell transcripts by qRT-PCR and single-cell RNA-seq. VCD-treated mice showed normal metabolic health. Compared with controls, VCD-treated females exhibited a 5-fold elevation in serum pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels and near-normal thyroid hormone levels. Pituitary Tshb mRNA levels were reduced, and pituitary Gh, Prl, and Pomc mRNA levels were unchanged. Serum growth hormone (GH) levels were higher in VCD-treated mice than in controls 62 days after the start of treatment (perimenopause) and then reduced to control levels after 118-138 days. Ingenuity Pathway Analyses (IPA) of upregulated differentially expressed gene (DEG) transcripts predicted activation of G protein-mediated signaling pathways in one scRNA-seq somatotrope subcluster and in the thyrotrope and lactotrope clusters. In contrast, downregulated DEGs in corticotropes and the remaining two somatotrope clusters predicted downregulation of critical signaling pathways. The unchanged pituitary Gh, Prl, and Pomc mRNA levels correlated with unchanged serum levels. The interim rise in serum GH 62 days after treatment agrees with reports of perimenopausal responses due to estrogen spikes. Reduced pituitary Tshb correlates with the recently reported reduced expression in gonadotropes. IPA analysis of upregulated DEGs in thyrotrope clusters predicted the activation of canonical signaling pathways that support elevated serum TSH levels. The near-normal thyroid hormone levels suggest subclinical hypothyroidism in menopausal women. Downregulated DEGs in corticotropes and in two somatotrope subclusters predicted compromised stress and metabolic responses. Finally, reduced multihormone gene expression suggested compromised plasticity in a low-estrogen environment. These different responses to a sustained low-estrogen state, such as that seen in menopause, reflect the diversity of estrogen's trophic actions.

title: FAM50A promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression via splicing-dependent oncogenic circSDK1- and DUSP22-mediated MAPK/FAK activation.
abstract: Dysregulated splicing factors play critical roles in tumor progression. Here, we identify family with sequence similarity 50 member A (FAM50A) as a pivotal oncogenic splicing factor involved in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Multi-omics and multi-cohort analyses revealed that FAM50A is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with a poor prognosis. Functional studies demonstrated that FAM50A promotes ESCC proliferation and migration both in vitro and in vivo, primarily through the activation of mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs) and focal adhesion kinase (FAK). We further characterized the FAM50A-binding RNA motif and established its transcriptome-wide splicing landscape. Notably, we identified a novel FAM50A-dependent backsplicing event that generates circSDK1, which originates from exons 2-4 of the sidekick cell adhesion molecule 1 (SDK1) pre-mRNA. Mechanistically, circSDK1 binds to dual-specificity phosphatase 22 (DUSP22) and occupies its phosphatase domain, inhibiting the DUSP22-mediated dephosphorylation of MAPKs and FAK and thereby sustaining their activation. Furthermore, the transcription factor TFAP2C increased FAM50A expression. Finally, we identified rifabutin as a small-molecule inhibitor of FAM50A and confirmed its anti-tumor efficacy in cell-derived xenograft, patient-derived organoid, and patient-derived xenograft models. In summary, FAM50A promotes ESCC progression via the FAM50A/circSDK1/DUSP22 axis, leading to MAPKs and FAK activation. Genetic or pharmacological targeting of FAM50A with rifabutin represents a promising therapeutic strategy for ESCC.

title: Ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: evidence from human peripheral blood and mouse brain.
abstract: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) has high morbidity and mortality. Ferroptosis may contribute to aSAH-related brain injury, but its peripheral and brain-associated signatures remain unclear. Human peripheral-blood dataset GSE36791 (43 aSAH, 18 controls) was analyzed using limma, FerrDb intersection, WGCNA, GO/KEGG enrichment, and PPI-based prioritization. qPCR validation was performed in peripheral blood from 10 aSAH patients and 10 non-SAH controls; aSAH samples were collected within 24 h after rupture. Mean ages were 60.2 ± 7.7 and 63.6 ± 8.9 years, with 5 and 4 males, respectively. Brain-level validation used GSE79416 mouse cortex and OMIX006611 mouse SAH single-cell RNA-seq data. Male C57BL/6 J mice (8 weeks, 20-22 g) underwent cisterna magna autologous blood injection; brain tissues were collected 1 day after SAH (n = 6/group). Immune infiltration and molecular docking were also performed. Among 2,645 DEGs, 35 were ferroptosis-related. MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD were prioritized as ferroptosis-associated candidate genes and were upregulated in human aSAH peripheral blood, mouse SAH cortex, and the clinical qPCR cohort. Single-cell analysis showed expression of the corresponding mouse genes across annotated brain cell types, especially immune/glial populations. In mouse SAH brain tissue, MAPK3/ERK1, STAT3, PGD, and G6PD protein levels increased, p-STAT3/STAT3 ratio was elevated, MDA content increased, and GPX4 activity decreased. Immune profiling showed increased neutrophils, mast cells, and activated dendritic cells. Ganoderic acid A was prioritized as a preliminary in silico candidate. MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD are ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aSAH, supported by human peripheral-blood, mouse cortex, single-cell, and mouse brain validation. Ganoderic acid A remains an exploratory in silico candidate requiring further functional validation.

title: Machine learning-derived R-loop-related diagnostic signature for psoriasis: a multi-cohort and single-cell validation study.
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by dysregulated immune responses and keratinocyte (KC) hyperproliferation. Although therapeutic strategies have advanced considerably, achieving durable long-term remission remains challenging. R-loops are three-stranded nucleic acid structures involved in genomic stability and inflammatory regulation in multiple diseases; however, their role in psoriasis remains poorly understood. To investigate the involvement of R-loops in psoriasis, develop an R-loop-related diagnostic signature, and identify key molecular drivers of disease pathogenesis. Transcriptomic data from five public bulk RNA expression cohorts (GSE30999, GSE41664, GSE13355, GSE6710, and GSE14905) and one single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset (GSE173706) were integrated for analysis of psoriatic and non-lesional skin samples. R-loop-related differentially expressed genes were identified and used to construct an R-loop-related diagnostic signature (RRDS) using the Elastic Net machine learning algorithm. Model performance was evaluated using three complementary analytical approaches, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed to quantify the contribution of individual genes. scRNA-seq data were further analyzed to validate the findings at the cellular level. In addition, the biological function of SRPK1 was examined in HaCaT cells by siRNA-mediated knockdown, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), and Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assays. R-loop activity was significantly elevated in psoriatic lesions compared with non-lesional skin. We established and validated an eight-gene RRDS that accurately distinguished psoriatic from healthy skin. SHAP analysis identified SRPK1 as the most influential feature in the diagnostic model. Single-cell analysis further localized SRPK1 to a pathogenic KC_4 subpopulation at a critical stage of keratinocyte differentiation. Functional validation in HaCaT cells confirmed efficient SRPK1 knockdown by qRT-PCR and demonstrated that SRPK1 silencing significantly suppressed keratinocyte proliferation over 96 hours, as determined by CCK-8 assays (P < 0.001). This study provides the first evidence linking R-loop dysregulation to psoriasis. We developed a R-loop-related diagnostic signature and identified SRPK1 as a potential key driver of psoriasis pathogenesis. Together with the in vitro findings, these results suggest that SRPK1 may serve as both a promising diagnostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target in psoriasis.
